headline: Refugee registration system launched but work permits remain unissued
context: Malaysia began its refugee registration scheme, the DPP, on 1 January 2026, piloting it in detention centres holding over 21,000 migrants and refugees. Work permits for 3D sectors, proposed in 2023, are not yet operative. Thailand has moved ahead on actual permits.

changes.summary: Correction: Earlier editions said 3,200 children were detained; the Home Minister's figure was 2,196 in August 2025. We also corrected when 37,000 people were screened (by July 2025, before launch), replaced a claim that case law extends the Employment Act to refugees, and removed unsourced claims about Sabah, state objections, religion and where registration takes place.

Correction: we removed two predictions no source supports, that no coalition would expand refugee protection beyond the registration scheme and that the scheme is the most Malaysian politics can produce.

cards.big: Malaysia's new refugee registration scheme went live on 1 January 2026. Work permits are proposed but unissued. Thailand has already moved ahead.
cards.sub: By July 2025, months before launch, 37,000 people had been screened, the Home Minister said. The scheme starts in detention centres.

cards.big: A 2019 IDEAS study projected that refugees with the right to work would add over RM3B to GDP by 2024.
cards.sub: The Malaysian Employers Federation backs work rights in shortage sectors. In 2025 the Home Ministry planned to register refugees at Immigration's 78 offices nationwide.

cards.big: Immigration detention centres held over 21,000 migrants and refugees in March 2026, Fortify Rights said. In August 2025 they held 2,196 children, the Home Minister said.
cards.sub: The Industrial Court awarded a refugee worker RM33,000 in unpaid wages (Asylum Access, 2023). The Immigration Act has not changed.

cards.big: The 3D jobs proposed in 2023 cover manufacturing, mining and construction. Domestic work and plantations sit outside them.
cards.sub: The US State Department's 2025 trafficking report flags forced labour on palm oil plantations and among domestic workers.

cards.big: Registration serves the state and employers first. The test is whether the DPP becomes a floor or a ceiling.
Whatever its political limits, the task now is making the DPP function as actual protection.
